[id="environment-variables-for-external-s3-files-provider_{context}"]
= Environment variables for the external S3-compatible files provider

[role="_abstract"]
You can configure the `remote::s3` files provider by setting environment variables in the `LlamaStackDistribution` custom resource (CR).
The following table lists all environment variables that the provider recognizes, their default values, and whether each variable is required.
Variables that contain credentials must be stored in a Kubernetes secret and referenced by using `secretKeyRef` in the CR.

.Environment variables for the `remote::s3` files provider
[cols="2,1,1,1,1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Variable
|Type
|Default
|Required
|Sensitive
|Description

|`ENABLE_S3`
|String
|Not set (provider disabled)
|Yes
|No
|Enables the `remote::s3` files provider.
Set to `"true"` to enable the provider.

|`S3_BUCKET_NAME`
|String
|None
|Yes, when `ENABLE_S3` is `"true"`
|No
|Specifies the name of the S3 bucket where file content is stored.
S3 bucket names must be globally unique.
The bucket must exist before the provider starts, unless `S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET` is set to `"true"`.

|`S3_ENDPOINT_URL`
|String (URL)
|None
|No
|No
|Specifies the endpoint URL for S3-compatible backends other than AWS S3, for example, `\https://minio.example.com:9000`.
Omit this variable when you use AWS S3.
Set this variable for MinIO, Ceph Object Gateway, OCI Object Storage, or other S3-compatible backends.
For more information about endpoint URL formats, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#overview-of-object-storage-endpoints_rag[Overview of object storage endpoints].

|`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
|String
|`us-east-1` (via `run.yaml` substitution)
|No
|No
|Specifies the AWS region for the S3 bucket, for example, `us-east-1`.
For non-AWS backends, set this value to match the region configuration of your backend, if it requires one.
The default of `us-east-1` is appropriate for many S3-compatible backends, including MinIO.
The recognized variable is `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`. The `AWS_REGION` variable is not used by this provider.

|`S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET`
|String
|`"false"`
|No
|No
|When set to `"true"`, allows the provider to create the S3 bucket automatically at startup if the bucket does not exist.
Requires the `s3:CreateBucket` IAM permission.
{org-name} recommends pre-creating the bucket administratively rather than enabling automatic bucket creation in production environments.

|`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
|String
|None
|Conditional
|Yes
|Specifies the access key ID for the S3-compatible storage backend.
Required unless you use IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) for authentication.
Store this value in a Kubernetes secret.

|`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
|String
|None
|Conditional
|Yes
|Specifies the secret access key for the S3-compatible storage backend.
Required unless you use IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) for authentication.
Store this value in a Kubernetes secret.
|===

[NOTE]
====
The `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables are shared with the `remote::bedrock` inference provider.
If you use both the `remote::s3` files provider and the `remote::bedrock` inference provider, and you require different credentials for each, use IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) or a non-AWS S3-compatible backend.
====

[NOTE]
====
For production deployments, {org-name} recommends authenticating to AWS S3 by using IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) rather than static access keys.
When you use an IAM role, omit the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables, and bind the IAM role to the service account that the Llama Stack pod uses.
IRSA-based authentication has not been validated by {org-name} Quality Engineering for this provider.
====
